restaurant_name: Le Louis XV - Alain Ducasse à l'Hôtel de Paris
description: Monaco's defining gastronomic address remains one of Europe's great temples of Riviera luxury. Alain Ducasse's dining room at the Hôtel de Paris turns Mediterranean produce, palace service and an extraordinary cellar into a benchmark special-occasion dinner on Casino Square.
highlights: Three-star Ducasse flagship, grand Hôtel de Paris setting, Mediterranean haute cuisine and one of the Riviera's deepest cellars.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; La Liste 2026; Gault&Millau; Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune

description: Just over the French border in Menton, Mirazur is close enough to function as a true Monaco destination dinner. Mauro Colagreco's garden-led, sea-facing restaurant remains a Riviera pilgrimage for affluent diners seeking the region's most internationally celebrated table.
highlights: Three-star Menton destination with sea views, biodynamic gardens, Mauro Colagreco's cuisine and top-tier global recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; La Liste 2026; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Official restaurant website

description: Marcel Ravin gives Monaco one of its most distinctive fine-dining identities, blending Caribbean memory, Riviera produce and polished resort hospitality. The dining room's Larvotto setting and tropical-modern energy make it a warmer, more personal alternative to Monaco's palace classics.
highlights: Two-star cuisine by Marcel Ravin, Caribbean-Mediterranean signatures, resort terrace and affluent Larvotto clientele.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune; Food & Wine

description: Les Ambassadeurs has re-established the Hôtel Métropole as one of Monaco's serious haute-cuisine addresses. Christophe Cussac's cooking is classical, luxurious and highly polished, with a dining room that suits formal celebrations, business dinners and old-school Monte-Carlo elegance.
highlights: Two-star palace dining, Christophe Cussac's refined French cuisine and an elegant Hôtel Métropole setting near Casino Square.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Hôtel Métropole Monte-Carlo; Monaco Tribune

description: Yannick Alléno and sushi master Yasunari Okazaki bring a rarefied Japanese counter experience to the Hôtel Hermitage. It is Monaco's most precise luxury sushi address, built for diners who want omakase-level craft inside a grand Monte-Carlo hotel environment.
highlights: Two-star Japanese fine dining, intimate counter format, Alléno-Okazaki collaboration and Hôtel Hermitage polish.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune; Food & Wine

description: High above the sea in Èze, La Chèvre d'Or is one of the most natural Monaco-side detours for a grand Riviera dinner. The draw is the combination of two-star cooking, medieval village drama, terraced views and the kind of romantic setting luxury travelers remember.
highlights: Two-star Èze destination with panoramic terraces, village glamour and polished Riviera cuisine within Monaco's luxury catchment.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Château de la Chèvre d'Or; Riviera Edition

description: Elsa gives the Monte-Carlo Beach a lighter, sea-breeze expression of Riviera luxury. Marcel Ravin's organic-minded Mediterranean cooking and the resort's water's-edge glamour make it one of the most atmospheric one-star dinners in the Monaco orbit.
highlights: One-star seaside fine dining, Monte-Carlo Beach setting, organic Riviera produce and Marcel Ravin's culinary direction.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune; Riviera Edition

description: Le Grill is the classic Monaco dinner for guests who want glamour without a long tasting-menu rhythm. At the top of the Hôtel de Paris, the room combines grilled meats, Riviera seafood, grand service and a roofline view that still feels unmistakably Monte-Carlo.
highlights: One-star rooftop classic, Hôtel de Paris service, rotisserie and grill signatures, sea and Principality views.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune; Food & Wine

restaurant_name: Pavyllon Monte-Carlo, un restaurant de Yannick Alléno
description: Pavyllon brings Yannick Alléno's counter-led, contemporary French format to the Hôtel Hermitage. It is less ceremonial than Monaco's grandest rooms but still squarely fine dining, with polished service, creative sauces and a format that works for stylish repeat visitors.
highlights: One-star Alléno restaurant, open-kitchen counter energy, refined French technique and luxury hotel service.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune; Food & Wine

restaurant_name: La Table d'Antonio Salvatore au Rampoldi
description: Hidden within the Rampoldi universe, Antonio Salvatore's starred table is the gastronomic counterpart to Monaco's famous Italian dining room. The cooking is more composed and ambitious than the brasserie below, giving affluent diners a refined Calabrian-Mediterranean tasting-menu address in the Carré d'Or.
highlights: One-star intimate table, Italian-Mediterranean tasting menus, Carré d'Or address and connection to Rampoldi's Monaco heritage.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Rampoldi; Monaco Tribune; Riviera Edition

description: Robuchon Monaco gives the Principality a renewed expression of the late chef's luxurious French vocabulary. The room's meticulous service, tasting-menu structure and Hôtel Métropole setting make it a serious current fine-dining choice rather than a nostalgic brand exercise.
highlights: One-star Robuchon revival, French haute-cuisine signatures, polished Métropole setting and high-touch service.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Hôtel Métropole Monte-Carlo; Monaco Tribune; Riviera Edition

description: Perched above Monaco at The Maybourne Riviera, Ceto is a design-led Mauro Colagreco address with one of the strongest dining-room views in the area. The seafood-focused cooking, minimalist room and luxury-hotel setting make it an easy Monaco-side alternative when Mirazur feels too far or too formal.
highlights: Maybourne Riviera dining room, Mauro Colagreco influence, Mediterranean seafood focus and dramatic cliffside panorama.
sources: 50 Best Discovery; Michelin Guide; The Maybourne Riviera; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Yoshi remains Monaco's most established luxury Japanese restaurant outside the newer omakase tier. Its polished Hôtel Métropole room, exacting sushi and discreet clientele make it especially relevant for affluent regulars who want a quieter, high-quality dinner near Casino Square.
highlights: Refined Japanese dining at Hôtel Métropole, sushi and robata focus, calm luxury atmosphere and strong local reputation.
sources: Gault&Millau; Hôtel Métropole Monte-Carlo; Michelin Guide; VisitMonaco

description: On the private Cap Estel peninsula between Èze and Monaco, this one-star table is a natural fit for high-end Riviera travelers. It combines a rare coastal estate setting with polished hotel service and contemporary Mediterranean cooking that feels appropriately discreet and privileged.
highlights: One-star hotel restaurant on a private peninsula, sea views, Riviera produce and a discreet luxury-resort mood.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau; Hôtel Cap Estel; Riviera Edition

description: Château Eza gives the Monaco catchment another highly romantic Èze option, with one-star cooking in a stone-walled village hotel above the Mediterranean. It is especially useful for travelers who want dinner to feel like a Riviera set piece rather than a city restaurant.
highlights: One-star medieval-village restaurant, sweeping sea views, boutique luxury hotel setting and romantic Riviera atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Château Eza; Riviera Edition; Gault&Millau

description: La Réserve de Beaulieu's grand dining room is one of the Riviera's great hotel classics and remains highly relevant for Monaco-based diners. The appeal is old-world coastal luxury: composed French cuisine, a serious wine culture and a terrace over the bay.
highlights: One-star Beaulieu classic, grand hotel service, bay-facing terrace and polished French Riviera cuisine.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; La Réserve de Beaulieu; Riviera Edition; Gault&Millau

description: Le Cap at the Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat sits slightly west of the Principality but belongs to the same luxury hotel dining conversation. The one-star restaurant is strongest for guests seeking formal Riviera elegance, garden-and-sea atmosphere and Four Seasons service.
highlights: One-star Four Seasons restaurant, Cap-Ferrat glamour, garden setting, sea air and refined Mediterranean-French cuisine.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Four Seasons; Riviera Edition; Gault&Millau
hotel_name_hint: Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel

description: The rebuilt Café de Paris is the essential grand brasserie of Casino Square. It is not a technical fine-dining play, but for Monaco it is a defining high-end social room: seafood platters, terrace watching, classic service and a front-row seat to Monte-Carlo life.
highlights: Iconic Casino Square brasserie, grand terrace, seafood and brasserie classics, high-energy affluent crowd.
sources: Monte-Carlo SBM; Food & Wine; VisitMonaco; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Amazónico has quickly become one of Monaco's most visible fashion-and-dinner addresses, especially for guests who want a lively night without abandoning luxury service. The rooftop position on Place du Casino, tropical design and Latin-Asian menu give it a distinct role in the post-fine-dining Monaco evening.
highlights: Place du Casino rooftop, lush design, Latin-Asian menu, cocktails and a glamorous late-evening Monte-Carlo crowd.
sources: Official restaurant website; Monte-Carlo SBM; Food & Wine; The Week

description: COYA is Monaco's strongest upscale Peruvian social restaurant, particularly in the warmer season. Its terrace, sea views, pisco program and polished party-adjacent service make it credible for a high-spend dinner, not just a drinks stop.
highlights: Seasonal Peruvian destination, sea-view terrace, pisco bar, ceviche and a polished Monte-Carlo social atmosphere.
sources: VisitMonaco; Monte-Carlo SBM; Official restaurant website; Food & Wine

description: Beefbar began in Monaco and remains the Principality's reference point for polished, design-conscious steakhouse dining. The Fontvieille room delivers premium beef, a strong wine-and-cocktail mood and the kind of affluent local following that makes it more than a global franchise address.
highlights: Original Beefbar address, premium beef, marina-side Fontvieille setting, designer interiors and loyal Monaco regulars.
sources: Michelin Guide; Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco; Gault&Millau

description: Maya Bay is one of Monaco's most established upscale Asian restaurants, with Thai and Japanese dining rooms that attract an affluent, international crowd. It works particularly well for stylish group dinners where atmosphere, service and menu range matter as much as culinary precision.
highlights: Established Thai and Japanese destination, polished Larvotto interiors, attentive service and strong affluent-local following.
sources: VisitMonaco; Official restaurant website; Gault&Millau; Food & Wine

description: Song Qi gives Monaco a refined Chinese dining room with a level of polish and pricing that clearly belongs in the affluent set. The restaurant is best understood as a sleek, special-occasion alternative to French fine dining for guests who want dim sum, Peking duck, wine and service in a composed setting.
highlights: Refined Chinese restaurant, elegant Larvotto room, polished service, dim sum, duck and an adult evening atmosphere.
sources: VisitMonaco; Official restaurant website; Food & Wine; Gault&Millau

description: Nobu's Fairmont address remains highly relevant in Monaco because the format matches the city's appetite for international luxury dining. The Japanese-Peruvian signatures, sea-edge hotel setting and glamorous bar-to-dinner rhythm make it a reliable choice for affluent travelers.
highlights: Japanese-Peruvian signatures, Fairmont Monte Carlo setting, sea-facing hotel energy and polished international luxury appeal.
sources: Official restaurant website; Fairmont Monte Carlo; VisitMonaco; Food & Wine

description: Em Sherif adds grand Lebanese hospitality to the Hôtel de Paris ecosystem. The restaurant's lavish mezze, polished service and glamorous Casino Square location make it a natural high-end alternative for groups who want generosity and atmosphere rather than a tasting menu.
highlights: Luxury Lebanese dining, Hôtel de Paris address, abundant sharing menu, elegant room and strong group-dinner appeal.
sources: Monte-Carlo SBM; VisitMonaco; Food & Wine; Official restaurant website

description: Rampoldi is a Monte-Carlo institution for polished Italian-Mediterranean dining in the Carré d'Or. It matters because it combines history, affluent regulars, serious spend and a room that still feels central to Monaco's social dining map.
highlights: Historic Carré d'Or Italian restaurant, elegant room, polished service and long-running Monaco social relevance.
sources: Gault&Millau; Michelin Guide; Rampoldi; VisitMonaco

description: Marius brings a more contemporary Provençal voice to Port Hercule under Sébastien Sanjou. It is valuable in the Monaco set because it offers a serious chef-driven dinner in a slightly less formal register than the palace restaurants, with enough polish and pricing for affluent diners.
highlights: Chef-driven Provençal cooking by Sébastien Sanjou, Port Hercule address, polished service and upscale local relevance.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gault&Millau; Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco

description: La Vigie Zanoni gives Monaco a seasonal Riviera dining address with real chef credibility rather than simple seaside scenery. Simone Zanoni's name, the Monte-Carlo Beach peninsula and the open-air setting make it a strong summer alternative for affluent diners seeking a relaxed but high-level evening.
highlights: Seasonal Simone Zanoni restaurant, Monte-Carlo Beach peninsula, open-air Riviera setting and upscale Italian-Mediterranean cooking.
sources: Monte-Carlo SBM; Monaco Tribune; Gault&Millau; Official restaurant website

description: Cipriani's Monaco address is not unique to the Principality, but it is highly aligned with the city's luxury dining habits. The room delivers familiar Venetian-Italian signatures, high service expectations and a polished international crowd near the Casino district.
highlights: Elegant Venetian-Italian dining, polished service, central Monte-Carlo location and strong international luxury following.
sources: VisitMonaco; Official restaurant website; Food & Wine; Condé Nast Traveler

description: La Note Bleue is the Monaco beach-club entry that most clearly combines a real Larvotto beach setting with credible dining. It is useful for affluent travelers seeking a relaxed dinner by the water, with live music, Mediterranean plates and a beach service identity rather than a formal restaurant mood.
highlights: Larvotto beachfront beach club, Mediterranean menu, live music, day-to-evening rhythm and relaxed Riviera atmosphere.
sources: Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco; Monaco Tribune; Monte-Carlo SBM

description: La Montgolfière is the kind of small Monaco-Ville restaurant that well-informed locals recommend when guests want something personal rather than palatial. Henri Geraci's cooking is rooted in local and Riviera references, making it a credible relaxed-night counterpoint to the Principality's luxury hotel circuit.
highlights: Small family-run Monaco-Ville restaurant, local specialities, chef-owner personality and proper dinner credibility near the palace.
sources: Official restaurant website; Michelin Guide; VisitMonaco; Tripadvisor

description: Les Perles de Monte-Carlo is a relaxed seafood institution at the edge of Fontvieille, loved for oysters, shellfish and its working-harbor identity. It is informal, but the product, setting and local loyalty make it exactly the kind of low-key dinner an affluent repeat visitor can appreciate.
highlights: Oyster and seafood institution, Fontvieille harbor edge, ultra-fresh shellfish and a relaxed insider Monaco atmosphere.
sources: Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco; World of Mouth; Tripadvisor

description: Castelroc is a fourth-generation Monaco-Ville institution facing the Prince's Palace. Its value is cultural rather than luxurious: Monegasque and Provençal cooking, terrace atmosphere and a sense of local continuity that balances the city's more international dining rooms.
highlights: Historic family-run restaurant by the palace, Monegasque specialities, terrace dining and strong local identity.
sources: Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco; Monaco Tribune; Tripadvisor

description: U Cavagnetu is one of Monaco's clearest traditional-dinner references, especially for diners seeking local dishes rather than an international luxury format. The appeal lies in Monegasque specialities, family hospitality and a relaxed old-town atmosphere that still feels meaningful for sophisticated visitors.
highlights: Traditional Monegasque menu, family atmosphere, old-town location and local dishes such as ravioli, farcis and fritters.
sources: Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco; Monaco Tribune; Tripadvisor

description: Le Petit Bar is a small Monaco-Ville favorite that works best as a relaxed, characterful dinner rather than a luxury statement. Its intimate scale, classic French-Monegasque cooking and local reputation make it a useful protected informal pick for visitors who want to step away from Casino Square.
highlights: Tiny old-town restaurant, classic local cooking, intimate dining room and strong word-of-mouth appeal in Monaco-Ville.
sources: Official restaurant website; VisitMonaco; Tripadvisor; local dining coverage
